sections.heading: Slate Roofing FAQs for Montclair, NJ

faqs.q: How long does a slate roof last on a Montclair home?

runs.v: About 60 to 150 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart; slate roofing can last over 100 years with proper maintenance, and the nails and flashing fail first.

faqs.q: Can individual broken slates be replaced without redoing the whole Montclair roof?

runs.v: Yes. Missing shingles and damaged shingles on a slate roof are replaced one at a time with a slate ripper, without disturbing the surrounding tiles.

faqs.q: Does a Montclair historic district require approval to reroof in slate?

runs.v: It can; properties in a historic district can need extra review, so confirm with the Montclair construction office before an appearance-changing reroof.

faqs.q: Should I repair or replace my Montclair slate roof?

runs.v: Repair when the field is sound and the failure is fasteners or flashing. Roof replacement is necessary for roofs with widespread damage, and NPS Preservation Brief 29 puts the line at about 20% of a slope broken, missing, or sliding.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for slate roof work in Montclair, NJ?

runs.v: It depends on the alteration type: re-roofing a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, while structural changes, or work over 25% of the roof area in 12 months on other buildings, need a permit.

faqs.q: How much does slate roof installation repair cost in Montclair, NJ?

runs.v: Most slate repairs run $500 to $2,100, a single tile $50 to $300, and flashing or fastener work $400 to $3,000, per HomeGuide and Angi; historic restoration runs $2,500 to $10,000-plus.

faqs.q: What is the biggest problem with slate roofs?

runs.v: On damaged roofs the stone is rarely the cause: the biggest problem is failing nails and flashing, plus harm from roofers who walk on slate or patch it with roofing cement.

faqs.q: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: Roofers treat damage over about 25% of a roof as the point where replacement beats repeated repairs; for slate, the NPS line is nearer 20% of a slope.
